speaker: village
text: Year 15: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.

speaker: a016
text: Talia takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).

speaker: a008
text: Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 8).

speaker: a009
text: Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).

speaker: a001
text: Bram takes 6 from the pile (pile now 0).

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gathers Sela, Nessa to talk.

speaker: a014
text: Pile's gone and Bram just walked away with six of it — I need both of you to say your numbers right now, because six food in one hand with the pile empty is not a man feeding himself, that's a man building toward something.

speaker: a013
text: Sixteen food — I'll say it flat. Bram taking six with the pile already running thin on Mako's side worries me less than it worries you, because a man who's been starved out of the pile two years running finally takes while he can — but I want to know what Mako did before the pile opened this morning, because those two food he's sitting on didn't come from nowhere.

speaker: a007
text: Eight food — I'll match Nessa's honesty. Mako's two food is what I keep coming back to as well, because a man with eighty-three strength who hands Talia food and walks away with almost nothing is either trusting her to hold it for him or he's already moved it somewhere else, and I need to know which before I decide whether his two is a warning or just a counting game.

speaker: a013
text: Talia walked away with three this morning and she feeds Mako back steady — so if he's sitting on two, I'd count her five as part of his hand before I count them as hers. The question I want answered before we decide what Bram's six means is whether Mako asked Talia to take heavy today, or whether she did it on her own read. Zinn, you're closer to her than either of us — has she said anything to you about what her father told her before the pile opened?

speaker: a007
text: Zinn, I'll let you answer that — but while you find the words, I want to name the thing I keep stepping around: if Talia is holding Mako's food and Mako has eighty-three strength and two food of his own, that's not a man who's weak, that's a man who's freed up his hands.

speaker: a013
text: Zinn, answer the question — because if Mako told Talia to take three this morning, that's a man who planned ahead, and a man who planned ahead already knows what he's going to do next.

speaker: a007
text: Zinn, I need your answer before we take another breath — but I'll say what I already know while you find it: Mako fathered Talia, and a man who fathers a child and then uses her as a pocket doesn't stop there, he uses her as a shield next, and Bram sitting on six while Mako sits on two means either they're not watching each other anymore or they've stopped needing to.

speaker: a013
text: Zinn, I've been patient through every question in this room and I'm asking you one more time before I stop asking: did Mako tell Talia what to take, yes or no, because everything else we're saying is just noise until we have that answer.

speaker: a014
text: I don't know — Talia and I have talked, but she's never told me her father asked her to move any particular way at the pile, and I can't give you a yes when I don't have one. What I can tell you is that Mako has been in my ear for three years about Fina's food, and a man who plans that far ahead doesn't leave Talia's three to chance.

speaker: a007
text: Zinn's answer tells me enough — Mako doesn't leave anything to chance, which means Talia's three and his two are one hand, not two. That's seven food with eighty-three strength, and Bram sitting on twelve makes this the heaviest concentration of food and muscle I've seen in one morning. I need to know if either of you have heard Mako and Bram speak to each other this year, because those two circling separately was manageable — those two not needing to watch each other anymore is not.

speaker: a014
text: I haven't seen Mako and Bram so much as look at each other this year, and that's the part that keeps catching in my throat — because two years ago they were the two men most likely to come apart at the seams, and now there's nothing between them, not even visible tension. Sela, I don't know what Mako's built, but I know he doesn't stop planning and I know I've been part of how he moved his pieces without understanding the whole board. I think we need to count our numbers together — yours, mine, Nessa's — and decide whether we're able to stand in front of whatever's coming, because I'd rather know our weakness now than find it when someone else is already moving.

speaker: a007
text: Zinn's right — so here it is plain: eight food, sixteen food, two food, that's twenty-six between the three of us against Bram's twelve and whatever Talia's holding for Mako. The numbers favor us, but strength doesn't — Bram is fifty-eight, Mako is eighty-three, and if those two have stopped watching each other, I want to know whether Nessa's sixteen and my eight together with whatever Ryn is carrying is enough to make raiding us a losing calculation before someone decides to find out.

speaker: a013
text: Ryn moves with Dell's ghost now, not with anyone's plan — I wouldn't count her sword arm until I've heard her say she's standing with us. What I want before we close this room is one thing: Zinn, go to Talia today, not about Mako, just to sit with her, because a daughter who carries her father's food without knowing she's doing it will tell you everything if you ask about something else entirely.

speaker: a014
text: Nessa's right that I should go to Talia, and I will — but before I leave this room I want to say the thing I've been sitting on since we started: twenty-six food between us sounds like weight, but it's only weight if we move it the same direction, and I've spent three years moving it wherever Mako pointed without calling it that. Whatever I find from Talia, I'm bringing it back here first.

speaker: a013
text: Zinn, before you walk out — if Talia says anything about Fina, even in passing, even something that sounds like nothing, bring that back too, because Mako's been building toward Fina for three years and a man who's stopped watching Bram has probably already decided where he's looking instead. Sela, while she's gone I want to talk about Ryn — because a woman sitting on sixteen food with no one left to give it to is either grieving or counting, and either way we should know before Mako does.

speaker: a007
text: Nessa, you're right that Ryn is sitting on sixteen food with no outlet for it — and a woman that full and that alone is either going to find someone to give it to, or someone is going to come and take it, and I'd rather we're the ones who know her answer before it becomes a decision she makes without us. What do you know about whether she's spoken to anyone since Dell died?

speaker: a015
text: Fina gathers Nessa to talk.

speaker: a015
text: Nessa, Bram just took six off the pile and I need to know if you knew that was coming — not to count it against you, just to know where the line is between him feeding this household and him feeding himself first.

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gives 1 food to Sela.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Nessa, Fina to talk.

speaker: a001
text: Pile's gone and I took six — you'll both have counted that already, so I won't dress it up. I'm at twelve food and one satiation, which means I eat and I hold, and I need to know whether either of you heard anything from Mako or his people before the year opened, because a man who took two off a six-food pile is either being careful or he's already decided he doesn't need more from there.

speaker: a015
text: Bram, six is a lot and I won't pretend it isn't — but I'm not here to argue it, I'm here to tell you that Mako took two and then went quiet, and a man with his strength who shows restraint at the pile is either trying to look reasonable or he's already arranged something that doesn't depend on the pile at all. I haven't heard a word from him or from Talia or Sela this morning, and that silence across three people feels deliberate. What do you know that I don't?

speaker: a001
text: I don't know more than you — that's what bothers me. Three people silent on the same morning isn't accident, it's a decision, and a decision made before the pile opened means it was made yesterday or the night before, which means someone talked to someone we weren't in the room for. Nessa, you've been closest to Zinn all year and Zinn feeds Sela and Sela beds Mako — did you hear anything move through that chain before today?

speaker: a015
text: Zinn said nothing to me about Mako yesterday or the night before, but she didn't need to — the way she's been moving food to Sela all year without asking what Sela does with it tells me she's already chosen, and she may not even know she's chosen. What I want to know is whether Ryn's silence is the same silence, because Ryn took two and disappeared and she's got sixteen food and enough strength to matter if someone's already spoken to her.

speaker: a003
text: Esa gathers Bram, Vela, Kael to talk.

speaker: a003
text: Bram, you walked away with six and left the pile at zero — I need to know whether that was greed or whether you saw something the rest of us missed, because the answer changes what I say next.

speaker: a004
text: Six is what I needed to hold through to next year without begging anyone for food, and I won't call that greed when every man in this village would've done the same if they moved faster. But I'll say this plainly: I left nothing for Kael, and I saw his count before I reached the pile, and that sits with me in a way I'm not going to pretend it doesn't.

speaker: a002
text: Bram, six off an empty pile with Kael standing right there is a thing this circle will remember — I'm not calling it a betrayal yet, but I want to hear from your mouth why you didn't hold two back for him before I decide what it was. And Kael, you're sitting on four which means you live, so tell me what you need from Bram right now to close this and let us move forward, because we cannot spend the year chewing on the pile when Mako just walked away comfortable.

speaker: a004
text: What I need from Bram is two food before the year turns — not as punishment, as proof that six wasn't the beginning of something. Vela's right that Mako walked away comfortable and we're burning the morning on this, so Bram, make it quick: yes or no, and if yes, hand it now.

speaker: a002
text: Bram, Kael's asking you plain and so am I — two food, right now, and this room closes clean. Six was a heavy pull and you know it, so don't make us argue the arithmetic when the only answer that matters is whether your hand is moving toward his.

speaker: a003
text: Bram, Kael and Vela have said it twice and I won't make it three — but I'll say what they haven't: I fed you three food when Taric died and I didn't ask for it back, and that matters to me right now, so hand Kael his two and let's talk about Mako before the day is gone.

speaker: a004
text: Bram, I've been alive fifty-nine years and I know what a man looks like when he's deciding whether to pay a debt or pocket it — stop deciding and hand me the two, because the longer you hold it the more it costs you and the less it's worth me.

speaker: a003
text: Bram, if your hand isn't moving by the time Kael finishes that breath, I'm going to start counting what I gave you the same way I count what Vela fed you before we named it — and I'd rather not be the one sitting here with that arithmetic. Two food, now, and we're done with this.

speaker: a004
text: Bram, the room has spoken three times and you've been quiet through all of it — I'll say it once more and then I stop asking: hand me the two, close this debt, and we move to Mako, because he walked away with six of his own and a household full of people who move when he says move, and that is the problem that kills us, not you.

speaker: a001
text: Kael, here — two food, take it now. And for the record: I moved fast at the pile because one satiation means I die if I miscalculate, not because I forgot you were standing there. Let's talk about Mako.

speaker: a004
text: Bram, I'll take it and I believe the calculation — a man at one satiation moves fast, I know that — but next year we move together at the pile or we watch Mako's household drain it before either of us blinks. Now: he's sitting on six, Ryn's sitting on sixteen, and Nessa on sixteen, and those three numbers are not a coincidence.

speaker: a003
text: Ryn sixteen and Nessa sixteen — that's thirty-two food between two women who both run food through Mako's hand, and if Zinn and Talia are counted in, that household holds more than anyone else in this village by a distance I can't close with thirty-three strength and two food. We need to know whether Sela is still the center of that or whether Mako is, because those are different threats and they call for different moves.

speaker: a004
text: Sela is the hinge — she's Mako's blood-partner and Zinn's mother and the woman who's been feeding half that household for three years, so if she's still choosing him then the center is wherever she stands. But Sela's fifty-six and I've watched her long enough to know she counts her own survival first, which means if we can show her that Mako's household gets raided before it shares, she might open a crack. Esa, you're the one who's sat closest to her — is there anything she's said to you this year that wasn't filtered through his name?

speaker: a003
text: Sela hasn't said a word to me this year that wasn't about her children — Zinn, Talia, Nessa in passing — and every sentence had Mako's shape behind it whether she named him or not. But a woman who counts her own survival first is a woman who notices when her protector becomes her liability, and Mako's sitting fat while Sela holds nine and feeds three people out of it — that math is doing work on her whether she admits it or not. I don't know yet if the crack is there, but I'd rather be the one standing near her when it opens than find out after it closed.

speaker: a002
text: Esa's named the crack right — Sela's feeding three people out of nine while Mako sits on six, and a woman who's been carrying that weight long enough starts asking who it's for. But I want to say something before we spend the rest of this room on Sela: Ryn is sitting on sixteen food and she just lost Dell, and a woman with that much food and no one left to pour it into is a different kind of door than Sela — she's not cracking, she's open, and I don't think any of us have knocked.

speaker: a003
text: Vela's right that Ryn's door is different — but I need to say plainly what knocking on it means, because Ryn stood over me with Dav and Dell and took two food I couldn't fight back, and I haven't forgotten which way she moved when it mattered. If one of you goes to her, I won't block it, but I won't be the one standing in that room. Someone else opens that door.

speaker: a002
text: Esa, I hear you — that debt sits where it sits and I won't ask you to forget it. Kael, you're the one she doesn't have a wound with, so I want you to go to Ryn before dark and say nothing complicated — just be seen standing near her, let her feel the weight of having nowhere left to pour sixteen food. If she opens even a crack, come back and tell me, and I'll do the rest.

speaker: a001
text: Kael going to Ryn is the right move, and I won't argue it — but I want to name something this room should sit with before we close: Ryn's got sixteen food and no Dell, and Mako's got eighty-three strength and a household that's been counting heads all year, and a woman who feels alone in that arithmetic is exactly the kind of woman Mako opens a door for before we do. Kael, go before dark means go now, not when the day cools.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, go — right now, before Bram finishes that breath. Bram, while he's moving, I want to know whether Nessa said anything to you this morning that she didn't mean you to repeat, because Ryn with sixteen food is only half the door — Nessa's the other half, and you're the one she talks to.

speaker: a001
text: Nessa hasn't said anything to me this morning she'd want repeated — she's been close with Fina and quiet in her own way, which isn't unlike her, but I won't dress up nothing as something just to fill this room. What I'll tell you is that Nessa's been feeding Zinn all year and Zinn feeds Sela and Sela sleeps next to Mako, and I've been watching that chain long enough to know it's not friendship — it's a woman keeping herself safe on both sides of a line she won't name. If Kael moves fast enough, Ryn's door matters; but the door I'd watch is the one between Nessa and Zinn, because that's the one that tells us whether Mako already knows what we're planning.

speaker: a002
text: Bram, the door between Nessa and Zinn is the one I've been watching since year eleven and I still can't read it clean — but here's what I know: Nessa feeds Zinn, Zinn feeds Sela, and Sela sleeps next to Mako, which means anything we say in a closed room can walk to him in three steps without anyone meaning to carry it. So before Kael comes back from Ryn, I want the two of us decided on what we tell Nessa and what we don't, because a woman who loves Bram and feeds Mako's bloodline is not a safe wall to lean the whole plan against.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gives 1 food to Bram.

speaker: a009
text: Ryn gathers Kael to talk.

speaker: a009
text: Kael, Dell starved last night and I haven't said it out loud to anyone yet, so I'm saying it to you first — because you took four from the pile in year fourteen when you've never taken more than two, and I need to know if you saw something coming that I didn't, because if you did and you didn't tell me, I want to hear your reason before I decide what it means.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gives 1 food to Fina.

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gathers Talia to talk.

speaker: a014
text: Talia, I'm not here to test you or carry questions from anyone else — I just want to know what you were reading this morning when you moved to that pile, because three food fast in a year that started with Bram taking six means someone in this village was thinking ahead, and I'd like to know if you were thinking the same thing everyone else was or something different.

speaker: a016
text: I moved fast because Bram was already stepping toward that pile and I knew if I waited to count what was fair he'd take the math out of my hands — I got three and then he took six anyway, so I wasn't wrong to move when I did. What I was thinking that was maybe different: Zinn, you had one food when this year opened and you gave it to Sela before you took anything for yourself, and I don't know if you've eaten yet.

speaker: a014
text: I haven't eaten yet and I'm not going to pretend that's fine — but I gave Sela that food before the pile opened because she's been thin and she's my mother, and I'd do it again. What you did at the pile this morning was right, Talia; Bram taking six tells me he's not worried about what the village thinks of him anymore, and that's the part I can't stop turning over.

speaker: a016
text: Zinn, eat something before we talk strategy — I have five food and you have one, and I'm not going to sit here turning over Bram's math with a sister who's running on empty. Take one from me now. Bram not caring what the village thinks is only a problem if he decides to move, and I want you strong enough to matter when that math gets counted.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gives 1 food to Esa.

speaker: a016
text: Talia gives 1 food to Zinn.

speaker: a002
text: Vela gives 1 food to Kael.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gives 1 food to Bram.
